analysis.title: Marketcolour + Flow / Luxury / Vallourec / ITM / Cross-Asset
key_insights: US equities rebounded sharply after choppy weeks: SPX +473bps to 7237 (best session since 9 Apr 2024), NDX +686bps to 26746, RTY +340bps to 2669, with 9 of 11 sectors up.
AI trade led the rebound on NVDA headlines: GS AI Semis basket +14% and GS Data Center basket +12%. European semis also rallied, GSSBSEMI +8.2%, ASML +8.9%, BESI +9.3%.
Momentum composition shifted: 12m momentum outperformed 3m and 6m momentum by the largest spread on record.
ETFs were ~37% of the tape, the highest since April versus a 5yr avg of 25%. Levered ETFs were ~$1 of every $4 of ETF volume, a record share.
US ETF short flows rose 8.5% Friday and 19% over the week, the 3rd largest weekly increase in a decade.
US pensions are modeled to buy $27bn of US equities, 83rd percentile over three years and 93rd percentile since Jan 2000.
Buyback desk activity was elevated at 2.2x vs 2025 YTD ADTV and 2.4x vs 2024. Mix shifted to 47% open market vs 53% 10b5-1.
Hedge funds cut TMT and added to cyclicals and defensives, with the largest net tilt increases in Financials, Discretionary and Industrials. HF momentum exposure fell to its lowest since early 2023.
GS retains Buy on Nvidia, PT $220 (35% upside), citing Huang's reinstatement as CEO and expecting a multiple re-rate, though pending investigations still weigh.
Cross-asset: GS is modestly pro-risk for 2027 and favours balance. Post sell-off 12m equity return potential looks more attractive and equity-bond correlations are expected to be more negative.
Luxury tracker: Buy LVMH, Prada, Moncler, Richemont vs Hermes, Swatch. Early Q4 trends are in line with 3Q26, US is strong, China remains weak after a steep Q3 deceleration.
Vallourec Buy, PT raised to EUR26.9 from 26.6 (~80% upside). Post-results sell-off seen as an opportunity and the valuation gap to Tenaris is expected to narrow.
ITM Power upgraded to Neutral after shares fell 61% in six months. The upgrade is driven by price performance, not fundamentals.
